ambitions.title: Four of the charter’s faculties
ambitions.text: The founding charter names six faculties. {school} has one of them. The Provost has proposed saying publicly how many will exist by a named year, on the grounds that a college which will not name a number has not really decided to be one.
ambitions.kept: Four of the charter's six faculties stand, which is four more than the year it was promised in.
ambitions.missed: The year named for the faculties came and went with the charter still mostly a document.

ambitions.title: A thousand students on the lawn
ambitions.text: Convocation is held on the lawn because the hall will not hold everyone, which is a happier reason than it sounds. The Registrar has worked out what a thousand would look like and would like to know whether that is the plan or merely the trend.
ambitions.kept: A thousand of them on the lawn, and the hall never used for it again.
ambitions.missed: The thousand did not come. The lawn was booked anyway.

ambitions.title: A hundred million in the fund
ambitions.text: The Investment Committee has done the arithmetic on what the endowment would have to be for {school} to stop worrying about a bad year. The number is not a secret and the committee would like it to stop being a private one.
ambitions.kept: A hundred million, and a college that can survive a bad decade.
ambitions.missed: The fund fell short of the number the college had said out loud.

ambitions.title: The best teaching in the state
ambitions.text: A trustee has asked what {school} is actually for, in the tone of somebody who has an answer ready. The answer offered, and minuted, was teaching: not the largest college, not the richest, the one whose graduates say they were taught.
ambitions.kept: The teaching is what the college is known for, which is what it said it would be.
ambitions.missed: The teaching did not become what the college promised a trustee it would.

ambitions.title: Not one building on the register
ambitions.text: The Clerk keeps a register of buildings with work outstanding. It has never been empty. The proposal is to say, publicly and with a year attached, that it will be.
ambitions.kept: The register is empty for the first time since the founding.
ambitions.missed: The register was not empty on the day the college had named.

ambitions.title: Owing nothing to anybody
ambitions.text: The construction borrowing has been refinanced twice and explained to the board three times. The Bursar's paper this year is one page and ends with a date by which the college could owe nothing at all.
ambitions.kept: The college owes nothing to anybody, for the first time since it broke ground.
ambitions.missed: The date passed and the borrowing is still on the books.

ambitions.title: A full catalogue
ambitions.text: The prospectus is thin. The Registrar has costed a full one — every programme the founded schools could offer, taught properly — and has attached the costing to a proposed date, which is the part that makes it an announcement rather than a memo.
ambitions.kept: The catalogue is full, and every programme in it is taught.
ambitions.missed: The catalogue is still thin, and the date the college named is behind it.

ambitions.title: A campus worth the photograph
ambitions.text: A landscape architect has been round and was polite. Her report says that {school} has buildings and does not yet have a campus, and that the difference is about fifteen years of planting and one decision.
ambitions.kept: The campus is what the architect said it could be, fifteen years on.
ambitions.missed: The planting was not done, and the photographs are still of buildings.

ambitions.title: Alumni who answer the telephone
ambitions.text: The Development Office has the figures on what proportion of {school}'s graduates have ever given anything, and would rather present them privately. The proposal is a decade of doing the unglamorous thing — asking about them rather than for money.
ambitions.kept: The ledger is warm, and the annual fund shows it.
ambitions.missed: The ledger stayed cold. The Development Office has stopped circulating the figures.

ambitions.title: Turning people away
ambitions.text: {school} admits most of who applies, which is not a criticism and is not a plan either. The Dean of Admissions has proposed the other thing: fewer places, more applicants, and the years of patience in between.
ambitions.kept: The college turns people away now, and the classes show it.
ambitions.missed: The college is still admitting most of who asks.

ambitions.title: Out of the hole by the decade’s end
ambitions.text: The board has been discussing the college's position for four meetings. This meeting produced something different: a date, written down, by which {school} will be out of it, and an understanding that the date will be remembered.
ambitions.kept: The college came out of it by the date it had named, which almost nobody expected.
ambitions.missed: The date came. The college was still in the hole.

ambitions.title: Thirty scholars worth the name
ambitions.text: The roster is small enough that the Provost knows everyone's field and most of their arguments. The proposal is to stop being that college: thirty of them, properly paid, in a decade.
ambitions.kept: Thirty scholars, properly paid, and a Provost who no longer knows all the arguments.
ambitions.missed: The roster did not grow into what the college said it would.

ambitions.title: Two thousand graduates on the rolls
ambitions.text: The alumni register fits in a single drawer of the Development Office's cabinet, and the Director of Development has measured the drawer. The proposal is to need a second cabinet by a named year, which means graduating people rather than admitting them.
ambitions.kept: Two thousand names on the rolls, and the second cabinet bought.
ambitions.missed: The date came and the register still fitted in the drawer.

ambitions.title: Students who would choose it again
ambitions.text: The exit survey asks whether graduates would choose {school} again, and this year the answer was a shrug with a percentage attached. The Dean of Students has proposed publishing the figure every year until it is one the college would print on the prospectus.
ambitions.kept: Asked whether they would choose it again, most of them said yes, and the prospectus says so.
ambitions.missed: The survey was published every year, as promised, and every year it said the same thing.

ambitions.title: Ten million in reserve
ambitions.text: The Bursar has been meeting the payroll out of the same account the payroll goes into, which she describes as 'working' and the auditors describe differently. Her proposal is a reserve of ten million, named in public, so that the next bad year is an inconvenience rather than an event.
ambitions.kept: Ten million in the reserve, and a bad year that passed as an inconvenience.
ambitions.missed: The reserve was never built, and the Bursar still meets the payroll from the same account.

ambitions.title: A hundred and twenty-five million in the fund
ambitions.text: The endowment has passed the point where it keeps {school} alive and reached the point where it could change what the college does. The Investment Committee has named the next number and would like the campaign to be judged by it.
ambitions.kept: A hundred and twenty-five million, and a college that can choose what it does next.
ambitions.missed: The fund grew, and did not grow to the number the college had printed.

ambitions.title: Twelve buildings, and still a beautiful campus
ambitions.text: The master plan shows twelve buildings where there are now a handful. The landscape committee has asked that the college promise, in the same breath, that the campus will still be worth walking through when they are all built.
ambitions.kept: Twelve buildings stand, and the walk between them is still the best thing on the tour.
ambitions.missed: The buildings went up, and the campus they were meant to sit in did not come with them.

ambitions.title: Two thousand students
ambitions.text: {school} is already bigger than its founders imagined, and the Registrar has stopped apologising for it. The proposal is to say how big it means to become, and to build and hire for that number rather than for the one it happens to reach.
ambitions.kept: Two thousand of them, and a college built for the number rather than surprised by it.
ambitions.missed: The college did not grow into the number it had named, and the plans drawn for it were filed.

ambitions.title: Alumni who come back
ambitions.text: Reunion weekend was attended by eighty graduates and a caterer who had been told to expect three hundred. The Alumni Office has proposed a decade of the slow work: letters that are not appeals, and a reason to come back that is not a building fund.
ambitions.kept: Reunion weekend has to be booked a year ahead, and the caterer has been told to expect more.
ambitions.missed: The reunions stayed small, and the caterer was told to expect fewer.

ambitions.title: Eight hundred students, and content
ambitions.text: Every college that grows quickly is told it has lost something, usually by people who were there before it grew. The President has proposed a promise with two halves: eight hundred students, and those eight hundred as content as the few hundred are now.
ambitions.kept: Eight hundred of them, and the survey says they would come again.
ambitions.missed: The college did not reach eight hundred students content with it by the date it had named.

ambitions.title: Borrowing under eight million
ambitions.text: The construction loans were taken out in a hurry and are being paid in no hurry at all. The Finance Committee has proposed a public target for the borrowing, low enough to be felt and high enough to be believed.
ambitions.kept: The borrowing is below eight million, and the interest line fits on one page.
ambitions.missed: The debt was still above the number the college had named, and the interest line runs to two pages.

ambitions.title: Twenty programmes in the prospectus
ambitions.text: The prospectus has filled out and the Registrar would like it to fill out further. Twenty programmes would make {school} the college a school-leaver can choose without first deciding what to be, which the Registrar considers the point.
ambitions.kept: Twenty programmes, and applicants who choose the college before they choose the subject.
ambitions.missed: The prospectus stopped short of twenty, and the date named for it passed.

ambitions.title: Teaching worth the fee
ambitions.text: A parent has written to the President to ask, courteously and with a calculator, what the fee pays for. The reply the board approved was that it pays for teaching, and that the college will show as much by a date it is willing to write down.
ambitions.kept: The fee is still high, and nobody writes to ask what it pays for.
ambitions.missed: The teaching did not become what the fee had promised, and the parent's letter is still on file.

ambitions.title: Five hundred students
ambitions.text: {school} is small enough that the Registrar knows most of the students by sight and some of their parents by telephone. The proposal is to be the size the buildings were designed for: five hundred, by a year written into the minutes.
ambitions.kept: Five hundred students, and the Registrar no longer knows all of them by sight.
ambitions.missed: The college stayed smaller than its buildings, past the year it had named.

lines.offered: The board has put something on the record: {title}.
lines.decadeBody: A new decade, and the board wants the college to say what it is aiming at. Choose up to {picks} to make public. Choosing none costs nothing.
lines.capReached: Three is as many promises as the college will make at once.
lines.note: A public commitment with a date on it. Declining costs nothing; keeping it is worth more than that.
